rows.question: Does this manual allow E20 fuel?
rows.shown_answer: Yes. The Fuel Specifications table lists the fuel type as unleaded gasoline with an ethanol content of up to E20, so E20 fuel is within the manual's specification. Failure to refuel can leave the motorcycle out of fuel and stranded and cause serious fuel-pump damage.

Using the wrong oil grade reduces the life of moving parts and seriously affects performance.

Always disconnect the black negative (-ve) battery cable first and then the red positive (+ve) cable when removing the battery connections. rows.question: My bike has been stored for over a month. Can I just restart it?
rows.shown_answer: The manual's storage precautions apply when a motorcycle will not be used for a month or more, and for re-use after storage it says it is preferable to have the motorcycle prepared through a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre so it is restored to its peak operating condition. The battery is the main concern. If the motorcycle is used very rarely and the terminals are not disconnected, the battery is bound to lose its charge and can end up dead. For storage of a month or longer, the manual advises disconnecting the battery terminals and removing the battery. Before refitting it, check that the battery voltage is within specification. If it is not, recharge it from an authorised service workshop or battery dealer. For checking battery voltage, the manual says to contact a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre or a battery service centre. If the bike was prepared with the manual's storage steps, those steps included draining the fuel from the tank and induction system and removing the charging circuit fuse from the fuse box. Anything done this way is part of the bike's stored state before you start it. This partly answers your question. The retrieved manual information does not establish that a bike stored for over a month can simply be restarted without preparation, and it gives no step-by-step restart procedure for a bike coming out of storage. It also does not give the battery voltage specification or say how to check it yourself. Always disconnect the black negative (-ve) battery cable first and then the red positive (+ve) cable when removing the battery connections. Caution: when connecting the battery, connect the red positive (+ve) terminal first and then the black negative (-ve) terminal. Caution: keep both battery terminal cables firmly connected to their terminals; failure to do so may damage the motorcycle electrical system. Note: poor contact or loose fitment of the battery terminals may cause ECU failure.

rows.question: The general warning symbol is on. Which exact part has failed?
rows.shown_answer: The manual describes the warning symbol in the tell-tales as an indicator that glows whenever a vehicle component faults. The manual lists the engine MIL separately: it stays continuously ON in case of an EMS malfunction, and the ABS lamp separately lights up for an ABS system malfunction. These are different indicators from the general warning symbol. This partly answers your question. The retrieved manual information does not establish which exact part has failed when the general warning symbol is on; the symbol only indicates that some vehicle component has a fault. Do not run the motorcycle if the malfunction indication remains ON continuously, as it can cause severe damage to the ECU and sensors; visit the nearest authorised Royal Enfield dealer to diagnose and rectify the EMS defect. The ABS indicator is ON during the initial check-up (until or after the vehicle has run a particular distance/speed) and turns OFF if the system is OK; it lights up again in case of any ABS system malfunction. Do not run the motorcycle if the ABS indicator lamp remains continuously ON.
